bull.b: Growing Elfabrio sales, additional geographic approvals, and European approval for once-every-four-weeks dosing support broader adoption of the commercial product. These regulatory and market-access developments can strengthen recurring product revenue and improve Protalix’s position in the Fabry disease market over the next several quarters.

The shift to meaningful net income and strong operating margins demonstrates substantially improved economics compared with the prior loss-making period. If commercial sales remain established, this profitability provides greater capacity to fund operations, support pipeline development, and retain more value from future growth.

A sizeable cash balance combined with no reported debt or warrants gives Protalix financial flexibility to continue commercial execution and advance its pipeline without immediate dependence on external financing. This conservative capital structure also improves resilience if development spending or revenue timing fluctuates.

bear.b: Dependence on Chiesi and uneven ordering patterns make reported revenue less predictable than underlying product demand might suggest. Shipment timing and partner inventory decisions can create sizeable quarter-to-quarter swings, complicating forecasting and increasing the business’s exposure to a key commercial relationship.

The large milestone materially boosted first-half revenue but is not a recurring product-sale driver. Comparisons may therefore overstate the underlying pace of commercial expansion, and future results will need to rely more heavily on recurring Elfabrio sales and other sustainable revenue sources.

The observed anti-drug antibody rate and unresolved choice between dosing regimens introduce meaningful uncertainty for PRX-115’s development path. Immunogenicity and infusion-related reactions could affect dose selection, trial progression, timing, and ultimately the program’s commercial positioning if they remain difficult to manage.
